application.cover_letter_markdown:
Dear Hiring Team,

My first real engineering project at Tuulikallio -- a 16-element ultrasonic beamforming array for pipe-wall monitoring -- taught me more about practical sensor-array work than I expected going in. Tuulikallio hired me in 2020 for my sensor characterisation background, and the array project pulled me deeper into beamforming, spatial filtering, and the whole problem of extracting usable measurements from noisy multi-sensor data. Over four years of that work, the signal processing side has become what I do and what I want to keep doing. Kaikuvaara's Senior Signal Processing Engineer role looks like the right place to take it further, and I wanted to explain why.

Day to day at Tuulikallio I am responsible for the signal conditioning chain across our condition monitoring products -- filter parametrisation, spectral decomposition for rotating-machinery diagnostics, and sensor-array geometry simulation for new product designs. The work is applied and hands-on, which suits me, but the product scope is narrow and the technical problems have become familiar rather than stretching. Moving to remote-sensing instruments at Kaikuvaara would mean harder problems in a more demanding signal environment, and that is the kind of change I am looking for at this point.

The three-week deployment I did in Oulu in 2022, commissioning the beamforming array at a pulp-mill site, was my first extended stay in the city. I liked the place and the pace. I have no particular ties keeping me in Espoo and would relocate without difficulty.

One practical note: although Tuulikallio operates in Finnish internally, all customer-facing technical documentation -- commissioning reports, product data sheets, training materials, integration guides -- is written in English. I have been the lead author on several of these over the past four years, including the final commissioning report for the Oulu deployment, which went through a formal technical review by the client's English-speaking parent company in the UK. Presenting technical work in English at internal reviews and customer handovers has been a regular part of the job. I am comfortable working in English and it would not be an adjustment.

The beamforming and sensor-array skills I have built at Tuulikallio are, I believe, directly transferable, and I would be glad to discuss the role further.

Regards,
Olli Saarinen

I spent three years working from Boreal Photonics' Oulu office between 2018 and 2021, and I came to appreciate the city's engineering cluster firsthand. Best regards,
Johanna Lehtinen

After ten years at Tuulikallio, the technical problems have become comfortable, and I want to be somewhere the engineering is genuinely difficult again. I am already in Oulu and available for an in-person conversation.

Tomi Laine
